name: Socrates
summary: Socrates wrote nothing, so all views come from Plato, Xenophon and others, and scholars dispute how far each portrays the real man. The reports show him obeying Athenian law even to his death while refusing unjust orders, doubting selection of officials by lot or ballot in favour of those who know, and preaching simple living and care of the soul. Where Plato may be speaking through him, as in the Republic, answers are low confidence.

notes: Born 470/469 BC, died 399 BC. Every answer is secondhand (Plato, Xenophon). Answers drawn only from the Republic are Plato's construction as much as Socrates' and are low. The Socratic problem is unresolved; the reports contradict one another. Later pass 2026-11-24: all new statements checked against Xenophon's Memorabilia, Plato's Apology and Crito; themes searched: government, means, world, economy, society, culture, liberty, ecology, technology. Nearly all new statements are not addressed in the sources and stay null.
